p1_meter.title: P1 meter
p1_meter.description: The sensor (in W) that reports the net power at the grid connection. A HomeWizard P1 meter can also be read directly: then the manager gets a new value every second instead of about every 5 seconds (the Home Assistant sensor remains the fallback). Leave the address empty to only use the sensor.

data.p1_homewizard: Address of the HomeWizard P1 meter (optional, read every second)

data_description.p1_homewizard: IP address of the HomeWizard P1 meter. API v2 (WebSocket, the meter pushes every telegram) is used with a token; the token of the HomeWizard integration is used when it has one.

power_control.title: Power control
power_control.description: How fast and how sensitive the manager follows the P1 meter. Change with care: a shorter interval means more commands to the devices. The P1 meter itself is always followed quickly; the manual interval only applies to manual mode.

data.power_start: Minimum power to start a device (W)
data.export_bias: Export margin while charging during changing clouds (W, 0 = off)
data.jump_w: Peak detection: P1 jump that starts a cycle at once (W, 0 = off)

data_description.jump_w: When the import or export grew by this much since the last control cycle (a kettle or hob switching on, or off while the batteries discharge), the next cycle starts at once instead of after the fast interval. A load that builds up is detected as soon as this much is added. The response of the batteries never counts as a jump.

slew.title: Direction change protection
slew.description: The inverter ramps its power by itself (about 250 W/s for a SolarFlow 2400 AC+), the integration does not limit that any more. A change between charging and discharging always passes through a confirmed 0 W and waits at least the delay below when 0 W is not confirmed. A started inverter keeps running at a low power for the minimum run time, so a short disturbance does not make the relay chatter.

data.flip_delay: Delay before a change of direction when 0 W is not confirmed (s)
data.min_run: Minimum run time of a started device (s)

lifetime.title: Multiple inverters: spread, roles and flash
lifetime.description: With several inverters, charging and discharging use as few inverters as needed (better efficiency): another inverter only starts when the running ones carry the spread threshold of their limit, and below it the power is merged back onto fewer inverters. The others stay ready for peaks such as a kettle. One inverter discharges and another one charges; a role only moves to another inverter when it leads by the role switch margin in SoC and the role was held for at least 5 minutes. The safe state stores 0 W once in the device flash, so an inverter that reboots starts at 0 W; it is written at most once per hour.

data.flash_safe_state: Store the safe state (0 W) in device flash
data.sleep_after: Let idle inverters sleep after (min, 0 = off)
data.ready_hours: Keep the discharger awake only at (hours, e.g. 7-9,12-13,17-19)

data_description.fill_level: Load per inverter before power is spread over one more inverter; below it, it is merged onto fewer. 85% with 3 × 2400 W: 1 inverter up to about 1900–2000 W. While clouds change quickly, 70% is used.
data_description.sleep_after: An idle Zendure inverter keeps using about 30 W while it waits for commands (smartMode 1). After this many minutes at 0 W it is put to sleep (smartMode 0, about 5 W); the next command wakes it, which takes about 1–2 s longer. The inverter with the discharge role stays awake for the next peak (see the hours below). 0 = always awake. Simulated with the losses of the inverters: about 850 Wh per day less in November, 230 Wh in summer.
data_description.ready_hours: With sleep on, the inverter with the discharge role stays awake to cover the next peak at once. Here you can limit that to the hours with the most peaks (local time, e.g. 7-9,12-13,17:30-19); outside them it may sleep too, and at the start of such an hour it is woken. Empty = always awake. Simulated with losses: about 120 Wh per day less in November.

device_ips.title: Device addresses
device_ips.description:
Fixed IP address or hostname per zenSDK device. It overrides the address from the cloud and from mDNS, which is useful across VLANs. Leave empty to detect it automatically. A GUESSED name means the cloud gave no IP: enter the IP address.

{devices}

diagnostics.title: Logging, simulation and test data
diagnostics.description: Debug options. The P1 recording writes every P1 value (every second with a directly read HomeWizard P1 meter) with the battery power to <config>/zendure_ha/p1_<date>.csv, as test data for the simulation. With the control state, every line also shows what the manager and every device did, and events_<date>.csv lists changes of direction, commands, mode changes and warnings. It switches itself off at midnight; older days are compressed.

data.p1_record: Record P1 every second until midnight (test data)
data.p1_record_detail: Record the control state too (mode, setpoint, cycles, roles and every device; about 2.5 times larger)

p1_token.title: HomeWizard P1 meter: token
p1_token.description:
To read the P1 meter at {host} via API v2, a token is needed. Press the button on the P1 meter and click Submit within 30 seconds.

Or tick API v1: then the meter is read every second via the Local API (switch "Local API" on in the HomeWizard app).

data.use_v1: Use API v1 (Local API) instead of a token

solar.title: Solar forecast
solar.description: Optional: a sensor with the solar forecast of today, e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_today (the hours from now on are added up) or sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_remaining_today. With it the batteries store every Wh on days they will not be full: the export margin during changing clouds and a negative P1 target are not used then. When (almost) no more sun is expected today, the inverter with the charge role is ready to discharge instead of waiting to charge. Leave empty to switch it off.

zensdk_unreachable.title: {name} does not respond
zensdk_unreachable.description: The Zendure device {name} ({address}) did not answer repeated local zenSDK requests. Check the power and Wi-Fi of the device, its IP address (Configure, Device addresses) and the network between Home Assistant and the device. The issue disappears when the device answers again.

mqtt_cloud_disconnected.title: Zendure cloud MQTT is not connected
mqtt_cloud_disconnected.description: Home Assistant is not connected to the Zendure cloud MQTT server {server}. Devices that depend on it cannot be controlled. Check your internet connection and the token. The issue disappears when the connection is restored.

mqtt_local_disconnected.title: Local MQTT broker is not connected
mqtt_local_disconnected.description: Home Assistant is not connected to the local MQTT server {server}. Check that the broker is running and that the user and password are correct. The issue disappears when the connection is restored.

zensdk_no_address.title: No address known for {name}
zensdk_no_address.description: The Zendure cloud did not return an IP address for {name}, so the integration tried the constructed name {address}, which does not answer. Enter the IP address of the device (Zendure app, device information, or the DHCP list of your router) in Configure, Device addresses. A fixed DHCP lease is recommended. Until then the device can only be used with the connection set to cloud.

p1_stale.title: The P1 meter sends no values
p1_stale.description: For more than a minute no P1 value arrived. The batteries keep their power for now; after 5 minutes they fall back to the base load of the last 10 minutes (only ever less, never more), so they do not export stored energy or import to charge. Check the P1 meter, its Wi-Fi and the HomeWizard integration. The issue disappears when values arrive again.

second_controller.title: Another controller changes {devices}
second_controller.description: The power limits of {devices} were changed several times by something else than this integration in the last 15 minutes: an energy plan or smart mode in the Zendure app, another integration or an automation. Two controllers work against each other, which costs energy and causes many extra commands. Switch the other one off. The issue disappears after an hour without foreign changes.
